stanza: I am sitting in the morning
At the diner on the corner
I am waiting at the counter
For the man to pour the coffee
And he fills it only halfway
He is looking out the window

counter.linePrev: "It is always nice to see you"
counter.line: Says the man behind the counter
counter.lineNext: To the woman who has come in
stanza: "It is always nice to see you"
Says the man behind the counter
To the woman who has come in
And I look the other way
As they are kissing their hellos
And I'm pretending not to see them
And instead I pour the milk

counter.linePrev: She is wearing rags and feathers
counter.lineNext: And the sun pours down like honey
stanza: And she leads you to the river
She is wearing rags and feathers
And the sun pours down like honey
On our lady of the harbour
And she shows you where to look
Among the garbage and the flowers
There are heroes in the seaweed
There are children in the morning
They are leaning out for love
And they will lean that way forever

She asks me how I feel today
I feel like Lovecraft in Brooklyn

stanza: I just wanna be my Dad
With a slight sprinkling of my mother
And work at the family store
And take orders from the counter

Pinballs and pool halls flashing their lights
Making change behind the counter in a penny arcade
Sat the fat girl daughter of Virginia and Ray, Lydia

counter.line: As we lay them on our granite counter top
counter.lineNext: We beat them up against each other
stanza: So we made the hard decision
And we each made an incision
Past our muscles and our bones
Saw our hearts were little stones
Pulled them out, they weren't beating
As we lay them on our granite counter top

counter.linePrev: I remember it all too well
counter.line: Photo album on the counter, your cheeks were turning red
counter.lineNext: You used to be a little kid with glasses in a twin-sized bed
stanza: Photo album on the counter, your cheeks were turning red
You used to be a little kid with glasses in a twin-sized bed
And your mother's telling stories 'bout you on the tee-ball team
You taught me 'bout your past, thinking your future was me

encounter.linePrev: The sky, the trees, houses, buildings, even my own body
encounter.line: And each person I encountered, I couldn't wait to meet
encounter.lineNext: And I came upon a doctor who appeared in quite poor health
stanza: The rain, it started tapping on the window near my bed
There was a loophole in my dreaming, so I got out of it
And to my surprise my eyes were wide and already open
Just my nightstand and my dresser where those nightmares had just been
So I dressed myself and left then, out into the gray streets
But everything seemed different and completely new to me
The sky, the trees, houses, buildings, even my own body
And each person I encountered, I couldn't wait to meet
And I came upon a doctor who appeared in quite poor health
I said, "There's nothing that I can do for you you can't do for yourself"
He said, "Oh yes you can, just hold my hand, I think that that would help"
So I sat with him a while, then I asked him how he felt
